An overview of B.C.’s Private

Managed

Forest Program

The Managed Forest Council is an independent agency responsible for administering B.C.’s Private Managed Forest Land Act and the Managed Forest Program.

Five facts about B.C.’s Private Managed Forest Land

Landowners participate in the Program on a voluntary basis, committing to protect 5 key public environmental values in exchange for certainty around growing and harvesting trees and the Managed Forest property tax classification.

1

PROTECTS 5 KEY PUBLIC ENVIRONMENTAL VALUES

Soil Conservation

Protect soil productivity by minimizing
the area occupied by roads and trails

Water Quality

Protect human drinking water
during and after harvesting

Fish Habitat

Protect fish habitat during
and after harvesting

Critical Wildlife Habitat

Protect soil productivity by minimizing
the area occupied by roads and trails

reforestation

Promptly regenerate harvested areas with healthy,
commercially valuable trees, not impeded by vegetation

2

ACHIEVES HIGH COMPLIANCE ON REGULAR INSPECTIONS

The Council Conducts

Inspections    |    Audits    |    Investigations

Owner Compliance Rate
0 %

Inspection Cycle: 1 Every 5 Years

The Council is authorized to enforce its provincially-mandated regulations by administering penalties, remediation orders and stop work orders.

3

FOCUSES ON CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT

COUNCIL ADVOCATES FOR SUSTAINABLE FOREST
MANAGEMENT PRACTICES CONSISTENT WITH THE ACT

The Council’s results-based model enables owners to use management strategies appropriate for and specific to their land. In 2019 following feedback, drinking water quality and reforestation regulation and requirements were enhanced.

4

GENERATES SUSTAINABLE ECONOMIC BENEFITS

B.C.’s private managed forests contribute to local economies and the province’s forest sector as a whole.

Did you know?

Managed forest land is a property tax classification designated by the BC Assessment Authority under the Assessment Act. The remaining private forest land is often classed as farm or residential land.
